}}

{{recipe}} 

Serve this with pork chops, or as a [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]].

== Ingredients ==
* 2 Honeycrisp [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]], cut into ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] wedges
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* ¼ cup unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* ⅓ cup [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]]
* Juice of ½ [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

== Procedure ==
#Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a large stainless steel [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] over medium heat.
#Add apples and cook, tossing often, until lightly browned around edges. Remove and keep warm.
#Add sugar, salt, orange, and cinnamon to pan. Scrape with a metal [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] to loosen browned bits.
#Melt in butter, 1 tbsp at a time, while whisking continuously. Once all butter has been melted, bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] (the fiercer the boil, the flashier the show).
#Carefully add brandy and, if it hasn't ignited by itself, do so with a long match or a firestick.
#Add apples and cook 1–2 minutes, depending on how soft you want your apples.
#Remove apples from pan and drizzle with sauce. Serve warm.

== Warnings ==

* Do not add the liquor directly from the bottle—if it catches, this can result in an explosion within the bottle.
